key_insight: Reliable protein–ligand binding predictions require reliable evaluation. Transparent data, code, and experimental procedures help distinguish genuine predictive ability from results inflated by leakage or bias.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks, and unclear evaluation procedures can make structure-based scoring methods appear more effective than they are and undermine fair comparisons.
method: Advocate transparent reporting and sharing of evaluation data, code, and experimental procedures.
Discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and reducing evaluation bias.
Promote fair, reproducible, and meaningful comparisons across scoring methods.
impact: These guidelines help AI/ML practitioners assess whether performance gains are credible and reproducible, supporting better-informed choices of methods for protein–ligand binding prediction.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand binding illustration showing a molecule fitting into a protein pocket.
Train–test split diagram highlighting how data leakage can inflate performance.
Transparency checklist with icons for data, code, and experimental procedures.
Balanced comparison graphic showing scoring methods evaluated under shared conditions.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
